mainTopic: Forgery concerns with a שטר written on erased paper (מחק), the ברייתא on text and witnesses on erased versus clean paper, and the start of רבי's objection to רבי חנינא בן גמליאל
overview: The גמרא defends רב's ruling that a שטר whose text and witness signatures are both on erased paper is כשר. A forger can't simply erase the text again, because paper erased twice looks different from paper erased once. To block a forger who pre-erases the witnesses' spot, אביי explains that רב requires the witnesses to see the paper erased before they sign. A ברייתא then says that text on clean paper with signatures on an erasure is כשר. The גמרא explains that this is only when the witnesses write a note saying so, placed between their two signatures. When asked why the reverse case (text on an erasure, signatures on clean paper) is פסול, it answers that a double erasure stands out only next to a single erasure, and here there is nothing on the page to compare it to. Every proposed test fails: erasures on other sheets differ, fresh erasures differ from old ones, and רבי ירמיה worries that courts will make mistakes with complicated procedures. Finally the גמרא turns to רבי חנינא בן גמליאל's view on a tied document, and רבי begins an objection that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Could the forger just erase the text a second time?
steps.stepSummary: An expected objection to רב: the holder could erase the text again and write a false one, leaving the witnesses' signatures in place.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say: he erases, and then erases again!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a possible objection to רב's ruling that a שטר written fully on erased paper is כשר. Couldn't someone erase the text again and write something new?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both text and signatures sit on erased paper, the paper already looks erased. So a forger could erase the text once more, write new terms, and the document would still look like an ordinary erased-paper שטר. The answer comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say: introduces an expected objection
An erasure; paper that had earlier writing scraped off

phrases.english: And if you will say:
He erases, and then goes back and erases again!
phrases.notes: He means the holder erases the text a second time, after the witnesses have signed, and writes a false text.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises an expected objection to רב's ruling (stated before this section) that הוא ועדיו על המחק is כשר.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that a שטר with both text and witnesses on an erasure is כשר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Since the paper already looks erased, a second erasure of the text could go unnoticed, which makes forgery easy.

steps.title: Erased once looks different from erased twice
steps.stepSummary: Paper erased twice looks visibly different from paper erased once, so a second erasure would be noticed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Something erased once does not look like something erased twice.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the objection. A second erasure would leave the text area looking different from the signature area.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After a second erasure, the text would be on paper erased twice while the signatures are on paper erased only once. That visible difference shows the forgery.

phrases.english: Something erased one time is not similar
to something erased two times.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical, physical distinction: the forgery would be visible
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A second erasure could not be detected on paper that already looks erased.
steps.terutzMaskana: Paper erased twice looks different from paper erased once, so the forgery would be noticed.

steps.title: What if the forger pre-erases the witnesses' spot too?
steps.stepSummary: A sharper worry: the forger could smear ink on the signature area beforehand and erase it, so both areas end up erased twice.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let us worry: perhaps from the start he throws ink on the place where the witnesses will sign and erases it. Then, when he later erases the text again, both this and that will be erased twice!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the last answer. A clever forger could make the signature area look erased twice as well, so nothing would look different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the witnesses sign, the forger splashes ink on their spot and erases it, so that spot is now erased twice. Later he erases the text a second time, and both areas match at 'erased twice.' This cancels the difference that step 2 depended on.

keyTerms.meaning: This and that, both of them

phrases.english: But let us be concerned that perhaps
he throws ink on the place of the witnesses from the start,
and erases it,
so that when he goes back and erases this,
phrases.notes: 'This' is the text of the document, erased after the witnesses have signed.

phrases.english: it turns out that both this and that
were erased two times!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 2 by describing a way to defeat the visible difference.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that 'erased once' and 'erased twice' look different
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the forger also erases the signature area twice ahead of time, both areas match and the forgery cannot be seen.

steps.title: אביי: witnesses must see the erasing
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that רב holds witnesses may sign over an erasure only if it was erased in front of them, so they would notice the pre-erased spot.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: רב holds that witnesses do not sign over an erasure unless it was erased in their presence.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the forger worry by adding a rule from רב's view: witnesses must watch the erasing before signing on erased paper.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the witnesses see the paper being erased, they would notice that their signing spot was erased twice while the text area was erased once. They would recognize the setup for forgery and refuse to sign. So the trick from step 3 cannot work.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds, it is his view

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that רב's leniency for erased paper depends on a safeguard: the witnesses themselves check the erasure.

phrases.english: Abaye said: Rav holds:
witnesses do not sign on an erasure,
unless it was erased in front of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the forger worry of step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adds a procedural rule that blocks the forgery
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A forger could secretly pre-erase the signature spot and fool everyone.
steps.terutzMaskana: Witnesses sign over an erasure only after seeing it erased, so they would catch the double erasure and not sign.

steps.title: A ברייתא: text on clean paper, witnesses on an erasure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that calls a שטר כשר when its text is on clean paper and the witnesses are on an erasure. It argues that, by רב's reasoning, this should be easy to forge.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: if the text is on clean paper and its witnesses are on an erasure, it is כשר. But let us worry: perhaps he erases the text and writes whatever he wants, and then it becomes a document with both text and witnesses on an erasure!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב using a ברייתא. It describes a forgery that would turn this valid document into the 'both on an erasure' type that רב accepts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the witnesses are on paper erased once and the text is on clean paper. If the holder erases the text once and writes new terms, both areas are now erased once each, which looks exactly like the document רב validates. So רב's approach seems to allow an easy forgery, yet the ברייתא still calls this document כשר. The answer comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection, usually from a ברייתא
Paper, here clean paper with nothing erased

steps.confusionAlert: The forgery here does not need a second erasure. One erasure of the text is enough to make both parts look 'erased once,' which is exactly the case רב validates.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:

phrases.aramaic: הוּא עַל הַנְּיָיר וְעֵדָיו עַל הַמְּחָק – כָּשֵׁר.
phrases.english: If it is on the paper and its witnesses are on the erasure, it is valid.
phrases.notes: 'It' is the text of the document, written on paper that was never erased.

phrases.english: But let us be concerned that perhaps he erases it,
and writes whatever he wants,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָוֵי לֵיהּ הוּא וְעֵדָיו עַל הַמְּחָק!
phrases.english: and it becomes a case where it and its witnesses are on the erasure!

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: הוּא עַל הַנְּיָיר וְעֵדָיו עַל הַמְּחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge to רב from a ברייתא, after the forger worry was settled.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that a שטר with both text and witnesses on an erasure is כשר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא validates text on clean paper with witnesses on an erasure. Under רב's view this is forgeable, since one erasure of the text produces a valid-looking 'both on erasure' document. So either the ברייתא or רב seems wrong.

steps.title: The witnesses write a note explaining the erasure
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא's כשר case is one where the witnesses write: 'We signed on an erasure, and the document is on clean paper.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The case is where the witnesses write this: 'We, the witnesses, signed on an erasure, and the document is written on clean paper.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from the ברייתא. The שטר is כשר only when the witnesses add a note describing exactly which part is erased and which is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry was that the holder could erase the clean text area and write a false document, so that both parts would look the same. The witnesses' note shows that the text area is supposed to be clean paper. If it later looks erased, everyone will know it was tampered with.

keyTerms.meaning: An erasure, a spot where writing was scraped off
Clean paper that was never erased

phrases.english: Where they write this:
phrases.notes: The subject is the witnesses. They add this line to the שטר themselves.

phrases.english: "We, the witnesses, signed on an erasure,
and the document is written on clean paper."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the ברייתא in step 5 by narrowing the case it describes.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא): the ברייתא is talking about a שטר with a protective note from the witnesses.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא calls any such שטר כשר, which seems to leave it open to forgery.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is כשר only when the witnesses wrote a note saying that their signatures are on an erasure and the text is on clean paper.

steps.title: Where on the page does the note go?
steps.stepSummary: Below the signatures, the note could be cut off. Above them, it could be erased together with the text.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where do they write this note? If they write it below the signatures, the holder can cut it off. If they write it above them, he can erase it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא checks whether the witnesses' note really protects the שטר. Each obvious spot for it seems easy to remove.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A note at the bottom of the page can be cut away with scissors. A note above the signatures sits in the text area, so the forger would simply erase it along with the text. Either way, the protection disappears.

phrases.english: Where do they write it?
If below the signatures, he cuts it off;
phrases.notes: "He" is the holder of the שטר, the one who might try to forge it.

phrases.english: if above them, he erases it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the answer of step 6 by asking how it would work in practice.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A place to write the note where a forger cannot remove it.

steps.title: The note goes between the two signatures
steps.stepSummary: The witnesses write the note between one witness's signature and the other's.
steps.simpleTranslation: They write it between one witness and the other witness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the note is placed between the two signatures. In that spot, it cannot be removed without damaging the שטר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cutting off the note would also cut off the lower signature. Erasing it would mean erasing in the middle of the signature area. So the note stays safe.

keyTerms.meaning: Between one witness and the other

steps.whatToRemember: The שטר with clean text and an erased signature area is כשר only with a note from the witnesses, written between their signatures.

phrases.english: They write it between one witness and the other witness.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Between the two signatures, where the note can be neither cut off nor erased without touching a signature.

steps.title: Why not save the reverse case with a note too?
steps.stepSummary: If a note can save the first case, the same kind of note should also save the ברייתא's last clause, which is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, look at the last clause of the ברייתא: if the text is on an erasure and the witnesses are on clean paper, it is פסול. Why is it פסול? Here too, let them write: 'We, the witnesses, signed on clean paper, and the document is on an erasure!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer using the second half of the same ברייתא. A note works in the first half, so why would it not work in the second half?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The סיפא is the reverse case: the text is on the erasure and the signatures are on clean paper. If a note from the witnesses protects the first case, a matching note should protect this one, and it should be כשר. Yet the ברייתא says it is פסול.

phrases.english: If so, say the last clause:

phrases.aramaic: הוּא עַל הַמְּחָק, וְעֵדָיו עַל הַנְּיָיר – פָּסוּל.
phrases.english: If it is on an erasure and its witnesses are on clean paper, it is not valid.
phrases.notes: "It" means the text of the שטר.

phrases.english: Why is it not valid?
Here too, let them write this:
"We, the witnesses, signed on clean paper,
and the document is on an erasure!"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the answer of steps 6 and 8 to raise a problem from the סיפא of the same ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that a note from the witnesses makes the שטר safe from forgery.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a note works for the רישא, it should also work for the סיפא, but the ברייתא rules the סיפא פסול.

steps.title: Blocking the expected defense
steps.stepSummary: The questioner heads off a possible answer. The forger cannot erase the text a second time unnoticed, because a double erasure looks different from a single one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now too, what would you say, that he erases it again? But you yourself said that paper erased once does not look like paper erased twice!
steps.whatsHappening: The questioner continues the challenge. He blocks the most likely defense before anyone can raise it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might say the סיפא is פסול because the forger could erase the erased text again and write a false one. But the גמרא already said in step 2 that a double erasure looks different from a single one. So, it seems, the forgery would be noticed here too, and the case should be כשר.

keyTerms.meaning: Is not similar to, does not look like

phrases.english: Now too, what would you say,
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are part of the corrected wording; some versions don't have them.

phrases.english: that he erases, and then erases again?

phrases.aramaic: הָא אָמְרַתְּ: אֵינוֹ דּוֹמֶה נִמְחַק פַּעַם אַחַת,
phrases.english: But you said: something erased once is not similar
phrases.notes: This points back to the answer given in step 2.

phrases.english: to something erased twice!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens the challenge of step 9 by ruling out the obvious defense, using the rule from step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling of the סיפא that the שטר is פסול.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The double-erasure rule from step 2 should expose any forgery in the סיפא, so there seems to be no reason to call it פסול.

steps.title: A double erasure is noticed only when there is something to compare
steps.stepSummary: The rule that a double erasure stands out works only when the signatures are on an erasure. When they are on clean paper, there is nothing to compare, so the forgery would not be noticed.
steps.simpleTranslation: That rule applies only where the witnesses signed on an erasure. Where the witnesses did not sign on an erasure but on clean paper, the forgery would not be known.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It explains why the סיפא stays פסול even if the witnesses write a note.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A double erasure is spotted by comparing it to a nearby single erasure, which here would be the erased signature area. In the סיפא, the signatures are on clean paper, so nothing on the page shows what a single erasure looks like. A second erasure of the text would therefore not stand out, and the forgery would succeed.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not known, it would not be noticed

steps.whatToRemember: Text on clean paper with signatures on an erasure is כשר if the witnesses add a note. Text on an erasure with signatures on clean paper is פסול, because a second erasure has nothing to be compared with.
steps.confusionAlert: The rule that a double erasure looks different is not dropped here. It still holds, but it only helps when a single erasure sits right next to the text for comparison.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the two halves of the ברייתא have opposite rulings and keeps רב's approach to forgery consistent.

phrases.aramaic: הָנֵי מִילֵּי – הֵיכָא דַּחֲתִימִי סָהֲדֵי אַמְּחָקָא;
phrases.english: That applies only where the witnesses signed on an erasure;

phrases.aramaic: הֵיכָא דְּלָא חֲתִימִי סָהֲדֵי אַמְּחָקָא אֶלָּא אַנְּיָירָא –
phrases.english: where the witnesses did not sign on an erasure but on clean paper,
it is not known.
phrases.notes: He means the second erasure would not be noticed, because there is no single erasure on the page to compare it to.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי מִילֵּי הֵיכָא דַּחֲתִימִי סָהֲדֵי אַמְּחָקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 9 and 10 by limiting the rule from step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting a principle: the double-erasure rule works only when there is a single erasure nearby to compare against.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A double erasure is always noticeable, so the סיפא should be safe and כשר.
steps.terutzMaskana: A double erasure stands out only next to a single erasure. Since the signatures in the סיפא are on clean paper, the forgery would go unnoticed, and the שטר is פסול.

steps.title: Why not test with an erasure on another sheet?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the court erase something on a different parchment and compare, to spot a double erasure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the court bring another parchment, erase something on it, and compare the two erasures!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a way to catch the forger. Make a test erasure on a fresh sheet and compare it to the erasure under the document's text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 said a double erasure cannot be noticed when the signatures are on clean paper, because there is nothing to compare it to. This step answers that problem: make something to compare it to. If the erasure under the text looks different from a single test erasure, the text must have been erased twice.

phrases.english: But let [the court] bring another parchment,
and erase [something on it], and compare!
phrases.notes: He means: compare the test erasure to the erasure under the document's text.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 11's claim that nothing is available for comparison when the signatures are on clean paper.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 11: a double erasure cannot be noticed when the signatures are on clean paper.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A comparison sample can be created artificially by erasing on another sheet, so the forgery could be caught after all.

steps.title: Different sheets erase differently
steps.stepSummary: An erasure on one parchment cannot be reliably compared to an erasure on another parchment.
steps.simpleTranslation: The erasure of this parchment does not look like the erasure of that parchment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the test-sheet idea. Each parchment reacts to erasing in its own way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Parchments differ in thickness and quality. A single erasure on one sheet might look like a double erasure on another sheet. So comparing across sheets proves nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: Of this one / of that one

phrases.english: The erasure of this parchment is not similar
to the erasure of that parchment.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the proposed test as unreliable
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A test erasure on another sheet would show what a single erasure looks like.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each sheet erases differently, so a comparison across sheets proves nothing.

steps.title: Why not verify the signatures, then erase them and compare?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests confirming the witnesses' signatures in court, then erasing them on the same sheet as a comparison sample.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the court verify the witnesses' signatures, then erase them and compare that erasure with the erasure of the text!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a new test that uses the same parchment, which solves the problem from step 13.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the court confirms that the signatures are real, they are no longer needed on the page. So the court can erase them as a sample on the very same sheet. Then a single erasure can be compared with the text's erasure.

keyTerms.meaning: Accept, meaning verify and confirm in court

phrases.english: But let [the court] accept the signatures
phrases.notes: To 'accept' signatures means the court confirms they are real. After that, erasing them does no harm.

phrases.english: of the witnesses in court,
and erase [them] and compare!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְקַבְּלַהּ לַחֲתִימוּת יְדָא דְּסָהֲדִי בְּבֵי דִינָא, וְלִמְחוֹק וְלִידַמֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repairs the flaw found in step 13 by using the same parchment.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 11: there is nothing to compare the erasure to.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A same-sheet sample can be made by erasing the signatures after they are verified, so the double erasure could be detected.

steps.title: A fresh erasure looks different from an older one
steps.stepSummary: רב הושעיא says an erasure made today does not look like one that is a couple of days old, so the comparison would fail.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הושעיא said: Something erased the same day does not look like something erased two days ago.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הושעיא rejects the signature test. The two erasures would be different ages and so would look different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new erasure of the signatures would be fresh. The text's erasure happened earlier. Age changes how an erasure looks, so the comparison could not show whether the text was erased once or twice.

keyTerms.meaning: The אמורא who gives this answer

phrases.english: Rav Hoshaya said:
Something erased on its [same] day is not similar
to something erased two days ago.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵינוֹ דּוֹמֶה נִמְחַק בֶּן יוֹמוֹ, לְנִמְחַק בֶּן שְׁנֵי יָמִים
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the proposed test as unreliable
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Erasing the signatures on the same sheet gives a fair comparison.
steps.terutzMaskana: The erasures differ in age, so they still cannot be fairly compared.

steps.title: Why not wait until both erasures are old?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests keeping the document for a while so the new erasure ages too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let the court hold onto it for a while!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to fix רב הושעיא's problem by waiting until both erasures are about the same age.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the only problem is that one erasure is fresh, time solves it. After a day or so, both erasures are old, and the court can compare them fairly.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him hold it, delay it

phrases.english: But let [the court] hold onto it!
phrases.notes: Keep the document an extra day, so both erasures are equally old.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 15 by removing the age difference.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 15: a fresh erasure cannot be compared to an older one.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Waiting lets the new erasure age, so the comparison becomes fair again.

steps.title: We worry that some courts will get it wrong
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה says such complicated procedures are risky, because a court might carry them out wrongly and approve a forged document.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: We are concerned about courts that make mistakes.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה closes this line of suggestions. Even if a careful test could work, not every court will do it right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rejection is not about the test in theory. It is about real life: a complicated procedure invites errors. So חכמים do not rely on such tests, and the ruling of פסול in the ברייתא's last case stands.

keyTerms.meaning: The אמורא who gives this answer

steps.whatToRemember: Every test for catching a double erasure fails: other sheets differ, fresh erasures differ from old ones, and complicated waiting procedures risk mistakes by courts. So a שטר with its text on an erasure and its signatures on clean paper stays פסול.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a general principle: חכמים avoid validating documents through complicated procedures that ordinary courts might botch.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said:
We are concerned about an erring court.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 16 and ends the series of suggested tests.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical concern overrides a theoretical solution
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Waiting until both erasures are old would allow a fair comparison.
steps.terutzMaskana: Courts might carry out such complicated procedures wrongly, so we do not rely on them.

steps.title: Quoting רבי חנינא בן גמליאל on a tied document
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a new section by quoting the משנה's view of רבי חנינא בן גמליאל about a מקושר whose witnesses signed inside it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא בן גמליאל says: A tied document, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new part of the משנה. It quotes רבי חנינא בן גמליאל so that it can discuss his view next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי חנינא בן גמליאל says that a tied document whose witnesses signed inside, as in a plain document, is valid. The reason is that it can be untied and turned into a plain document. The גמרא only gives the opening words and then says 'etc.'

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא whose view in the משנה is quoted
A tied document, folded and stitched, with signatures on the back of each fold
Etc., the rest of the quote

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥanina ben Gamliel says:
A tied [document], etc.
phrases.notes: The rest of the משנה line: a tied document signed inside is valid, because it can be turned into a plain one.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: מְקוּשָּׁר וְכוּ׳
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the erasure discussion and opens a new topic from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A tied document whose witnesses signed inside is valid, because it can be made into a plain document.

steps.title: רבי responds to רבי חנינא בן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces an objection by רבי to רבי חנינא בן גמליאל's ruling. The content of the objection comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי responded to the words of רבי חנינא בן גמליאל:
steps.whatsHappening: This line is a setup. It announces that רבי is about to challenge רבי חנינא בן גמליאל, and the challenge itself comes in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word הֵשִׁיב signals a reply or rebuttal, not agreement. Here רבי means רבי יהודה הנשיא. The content of his objection comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: רבי יהודה הנשיא, editor of the משנה
